- Model tends to overestimate prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates the subsequent correction or mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true outcomes in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or insufficient weight on recent data.
- When prices spike, model reacts with a sharp overshoot followed by a premature correction, missing the sustained upward trend.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the latter half of the forecast, indicating underweighting of recent high prices.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — model fails to adjust downward after peaks, leading to overestimation of future values.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: last 5–7 days are consistently underestimated, suggesting model lacks sensitivity to recent momentum or volatility clustering.
